messages:
Anna (CS): Drafting a tiny customer-facing runbook to paste into onboarding docs. Needs to cover quick readiness, two-step mitigation (cache/batch/stream), a pasteable SDK snippet, and a 24h feedback ask.

Mike (SRE): Keep telemetry to 3 checks: 95p latency, cache_hit_rate, error_rate. I'll add minimal PromQL lines.

Anna (CS): Customer copy (single block):

"Micro Runbook: Fast Start"
1) Readiness (2 min): confirm model pinned; enable prefix cache TTL=600s; set batching target=10, max_latency_ms=120; streaming=on.
2) If latency/errors appear:
  - Step A (0-5m): increase cache TTL to 1200s and recheck cache_hit_rate.
  - Step B (5-15m): disable streaming for the route and reduce target_batch_size by ~50%. If errors >1% for 5m, switch to fallback_model=redwood-lite-v1 and notify CS.
3) Pasteable SDK snippet: {"model":"redwood-boost-1","prefill_cache":{"enabled":true,"ttl_seconds":600},"batching":{"target_batch_size":10,"max_latency_ms":120},"streaming":true}
4) 24h pulse (one line): "Any latency spikes or quality regressions? Reply with route + sample input. If no, share expected peak users/day."

Raj (Customer): Nice. One quick customer question: when should we bump TTL vs add prefill entries?

Anna (CS): One-liner for customers: "Increase TTL when prompts are stable and reused across sessions; add prefill entries when short, deterministic fragments (greetings, IDs) appear at session start and reduce new-token compute."

Mike (SRE): Internal PromQL snippets for handoff: rate(redwood_infer_requests_total[5m]) by (route); histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_infer_response_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)); sum(rate(redwood_cache_hit_total[5m]))/sum(rate(redwood_cache_lookup_total[5m])).
